subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Rana Plaza Factory Collapse
description: Learn The Rana Plaza Factory Collapse in one minute.

hook.text: On April 24, 2013, Rana Plaza in Bangladesh collapsed, killing 1,134 garment workers. It's the deadliest garment factory disaster.

buildup.text: The building was designed for shops, not heavy machinery. Three floors were added illegally without engineering approval.

discovery.text: Cracks appeared the day before. An engineer declared the building unsafe. Factory owners ordered workers back inside.

twist.text: The building produced clothing for major Western brands. Consumer pressure forced brands to sign safety accords afterward.

climax.text: The Bangladesh Accord inspected 1,600 factories. Over 100,000 safety issues were identified and corrected.

punchline.text: Workers warned it was unsafe. They were sent back inside.

quiz.question: What was done after the Rana Plaza disaster to prevent similar events?
options: Bangladesh banned all garment manufacturing above two stories
The Bangladesh Accord inspected 1,600 factories and corrected over 100,000 safety issues
Western brands moved all manufacturing to countries with stricter building codes
